text_translated: Printed pp. 90-91: Angeli's salt decomposes to HNO + NO2- (5.24); stable above pH 11, half-life about 30 min at pH 9 (Dutton et al.). Row 1: no change of nitrate, so the HNO route was considered not to participate. Row 2: NO2- plays the catalyst role in the hydroxylamine reaction (5.19); nitrate fell only 5 %, so (5.19) can have only a small part. Row 3: with NO (NO2-free) passed through, nitrate fell 29 %, so nitrate reacts directly with NO by the Abel-Schmid reaction (5.18), although its known kinetics predict a very low rate at this pH. Text cross-references slip: it cites (5.23) for the Angeli decomposition and says '(5.24) has no participation' where (5.21) is meant.
